title: General paired scan loop
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with oracle, let $y$ be a bit string, and choose distinct registers $p,q,	ext{lim}$ and an oracle index $j$. Let $delta$ update a state using a pair of bits, and suppose the program's test state compares register $p$ with $	ext{lim}$, its first read queries oracle $j$ on the whole input paired with the binary representation of $p$, and its second read queries the same oracle using $q$ and updates the state by $delta$. Suppose each advance phase increments its respective register by one for exactly $	ext{stride}$ steps before returning to the next phase, where $	ext{stride}>0$. Given equal-length bit strings $u,u'$, an initial state $st_0$, and a valuation $v$ bounded by $B$, assume $v(	ext{lim})=v(p)+	ext{stride}|u|$, $v(q)+	ext{stride}|u|\le B$, and for each $i<|u|$ the oracle answers at the two corresponding paired inputs are the $i$th bits of $u$ and $u'$ (with out-of-range bits false). Then the program has a finite execution from the test state with state $st_0$ to the done state with state obtained by folding $\delta$ over the zipped lists $u,u'$. The final valuation advances $p$ and $q$ by $\text{stride}|u|$ and leaves all other registers unchanged; the guard conditions hold throughout, and all registers remain at most $B$.
